messages:
sasha: Heads up — getting customer reports of 429s from the limiter on Dedicated pools around 14:04 UTC. They say traffic was bursty but well within committed throughput. :eyes:

mike-oncall: Which customers? any common model/region? logs?

sasha: Customer A (eu-west) + a few internal load tests. Logs attached below. Limiter started returning 429 with 'tokens=0' message even though we saw low sustained QPS after the burst.

sasha: ```
2024-03-02T14:04:12Z limiter.go:tokenLoop tokens=0 bucket=rb-prod-1 client=acct-123
2024-03-02T14:04:12Z limiter.go:refillInterval=0ms parsed_from_env RATE_REFILL_INTERVAL=0
2024-03-02T14:04:13Z limiter.go:tokenLoop tokens=0
```

alia-eng-runtime: whoa, refillInterval=0ms looks wrong. We changed how RATE_REFILL_INTERVAL is parsed in the last deploy (env var parsing). Could be a unit mismatch (seconds vs ms) -> parsed to 0.

kevin-support: Customer A opened a ticket, says they saw 15-20% error rate for 10 minutes, services autoscaled but retries still saw 429. I've already offered priority support and credits but need confirmation root cause for billing notes.

lucy-infra: Which deploy rolled the parsing change? I can pin the rollout and roll back if needed.

mike-oncall: @lucy-infra please check deploys at 13:58–14:02 UTC. If it's config parsing we'll roll forward a hotfix, not full rollback.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook suggestion: "If limiter tokens do not refill, check RATE_REFILL_INTERVAL and RATE_UNIT envs. Try temporary override: RATE_REFILL_INTERVAL=1000 and restart limiter pod."

sasha: Repro steps I used in staging:
1) run a 500rps 5s burst to the dedicated endpoint
2) wait 10s for sustained 50rps
3) observe 429s when token refill is zero

curl example:```
ab -n 600 -c 100 https://dedicated.example.com/v1/generate
```

alia-eng-runtime: I pushed a quick validation PR that rejects RATE_REFILL_INTERVAL <= 0 and emits a metric `limiter.config.invalid_refill`. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/limiter/pull/842

jordan-qa: Can we get a canary deploy to one dedicated pool and run the staging burst test? I'll run smoke after the patch.

lucy-infra: Starting a canary rollout to rb-prod-1 now. Command: `kubectl set env deployment/limiter RATE_REFILL_INTERVAL=1000 --namespace=dedicated-rb-prod-1` then `kubectl rollout restart deployment/limiter`.

mike-oncall: Patch deployed to canary. Jordan — please run the burst.

jordan-qa: Ran burst test — no 429s post-patch for 20 runs. :+1:

kevin-support: Customer A confirmed error rates dropped after ~3 minutes. They're asking for a postmortem and timeline.

alia-eng-runtime: Root cause summary for post-incident notes: during last config parsing refactor we switched RATE_REFILL_INTERVAL parsing from "seconds" to "milliseconds" but the envs in prod remained in seconds. The parser used integer math and truncated values <1000ms to 0. For example `RATE_REFILL_INTERVAL=1` (intended as 1s) became 1ms and then was truncated to 0 when cast, resulting in no refill.

alia-eng-runtime: Immediate mitigation we applied: validation to reject <=0, hotfix to treat values <1000 as seconds fallback, canary rollout. Medium-term: add schema validation in the operator and a config linting step in pipeline.

sasha: Impact: ~3 dedicated customers saw transient 429s for 5–12 minutes. We offered billing credits to affected customers and updated support ticket. No data leak / security impact.

prod-ops: We should also add an alert: if limiter.tokens_available metric == 0 for >30s and requests/second > baseline -> P1.

mike-oncall: Action items (assignments):
- alia: write postmortem and include code link + timeline (by EOD)
- lucy: add config schema validation to deployment operator (start this week)
- jordan: add an e2e test that runs a burst and asserts tokens refill (in CI)
- kevin: coordinate customer comms and credits (in progress)

sasha: Quick note about longer-term: consider changing default behavior so limiter uses a small fail-safe refill if config parsing fails (e.g., fallback to 100ms) to avoid total token loss on misconfig.

alia-eng-runtime: Agreed. I'll include that as a mitigaton. Also adding a debug endpoint `/internal/limiter/status` that returns `tokens_available` and `refill_interval` for quicker diagnosis.

kevin-support: Customer follow-up message drafted: "We identified a configuration parsing issue that caused token buckets to stop refilling during high burst traffic. A fix has been deployed and we will credit impacted usage. Apologies for disruption." Want to send when PM/legal OK.

mike-oncall: Final note — this looked like a subtle unit mismatch + int truncation. Need to add a unit test that ensures `parseRefillInterval("1")` != 0. :facepalm:

lucy-infra: Rolling the hotfix to all affected dedicated pools now (staggered). I'll post updated rollout status.

ops-runbook-bot: Post-incident checklist started: create postmortem doc, update runbooks, add alert.

sasha: thanks all. keep this thread updated with postmortem link and customer confirm. :raised_hands:
